summary: Defines the ZONEVERSION EDNS option, which lets clients ask an authoritative DNS server what version of a zone produced a response. The only version type defined here is the SERIAL field from the SOA record, though others can be added later.

eli5.summary: A DNS server is like a library, and a zone is one of its books. This lets you ask which edition of the book an answer came from.

questions: how to find the zone version of a dns answer
what is the dns zoneversion option
how to see the soa serial in a dns response
subtitle: A way for a DNS answer to say which version of the zone it came from.

tldr.problem: DNS data is only loosely coherent, and busy zones sit behind anycast or load-balanced servers, so two queries may reach servers holding different versions of a zone. That makes debugging hard.
tldr.mechanism: A client sends an empty ZONEVERSION EDNS(0) option (option code 19). An authoritative server answers with the zone's label count, a type number and a version value. The only type defined is SOA-SERIAL, the zone's SOA serial number.
tldr.outcome: The answer and its zone version arrive together in one response. The data is not covered by DNSSEC, so the RFC says to use it only for troubleshooting and debugging.

today: RFC 9660 is a Proposed Standard from October 2024. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why a Zone Version Helps
sections.content:
RFC 9660 defines the ZONEVERSION option. A DNS client can use it to ask an authoritative server for a token that represents the version of the zone a response was generated from. It is similar to the NSID option in RFC 5001, which identifies the name server that produced a response.

DNS data is loosely coherent, so one record can be out of sync with other authoritative sources of the same data. High-volume zones often use IP anycast or load-balanced backend servers, and nothing ensures that two separate queries reach the same server. Putting the version in the same response as the data removes that guesswork.

Support is OPTIONAL for both clients and name servers. The option is meant for authoritative answers only, for hop-to-hop use, and it is not transitive.
sections.eli5: If two helpers give you different answers, you want to know which copy of the book each one read. This puts the edition number on every answer.

sections.title: The ZONEVERSION Option Format
sections.content:
ZONEVERSION is an EDNS(0) option with OPTION-CODE 19. In a query, OPTION-LENGTH MUST be 0 and the data is omitted. In a response, OPTION-LENGTH is the length in octets of the data, which has three fields:

  • LABELCOUNT: one octet, the number of labels in the name of the zone the version refers to.
  • TYPE: one octet, which says how to read the version.
  • VERSION: an opaque octet string with the version data.

LABELCOUNT picks out the zone by taking the last LABELCOUNT labels of the original QNAME. For the QNAME a.b.c.example.com a LABELCOUNT of 2 means the zone example.com.. It does not count the terminating root label, it MUST NOT exceed the number of labels in the QNAME, and the root zone has a LABELCOUNT of 0.

This lets a client tell apart the parent and child zones in a referral, or two zones in one answer such as a CNAME and its target in another zone.
sections.eli5: The answer carries a little sticker with three bits of information: which book, what kind of edition number, and the number itself.

sections.title: How Clients and Servers Use It
sections.content:
A client MAY ask for zone versions by putting an empty ZONEVERSION option in the OPT pseudo-RR of a query to an authoritative server. It SHOULD NOT send the option to non-authoritative servers, and it MUST NOT include more than one ZONEVERSION option in a query.

A server that understands the option, is authoritative for one or more enclosing zones of the original QNAME, and chooses to honor the request puts a TYPE and VERSION in the response. Otherwise it MUST NOT include the option. A server MAY include several options, for different types or different enclosing zones, but MUST NOT include more than one for a given TYPE and LABELCOUNT.

The option should also appear on downward referrals (with the version of the referring zone), NXDOMAIN, NODATA and SERVFAIL responses from a server authoritative for the original QNAME, even without Answer section records.

A server MUST return FORMERR if the query's OPTION-LENGTH is not zero or if more than one ZONEVERSION option is present. The option is not transitive: a name server MUST NOT blindly copy it into a query it sends onward, and MUST NOT send it to a client that did not ask for it.
sections.eli5: You ask the librarian for the edition number by holding up an empty card. The librarian writes it on the card, but only if they actually own the book.

sections.title: The SOA-SERIAL Type
sections.content:
The only TYPE defined here is SOA-SERIAL, with value 0. Its VERSION is a copy of the unsigned 32-bit SERIAL field of the zone's SOA record, and its OPTION-LENGTH in responses MUST be 6: one octet of LABELCOUNT, one of TYPE and four of serial.

Some zones are distributed by other means, such as relational databases, where the SOA serial may say nothing about the content version. In that case a server SHOULD NOT send SOA-SERIAL. New types can be defined later, and zone operators may use the Private Use code points instead.

In presentation format, the type is written as SOA-SERIAL and the version as an unsigned decimal integer. The option itself is written with the mnemonic ZONEVERSION, and the zone name should be displayed alongside the label count.
sections.eli5: The first kind of edition number is the serial number the zone already carries. It is just copied into the answer.

sections.title: Example Output
sections.content: The RFC shows a dig query for the AAAA record of www.example.com with a zoneversion flag. The response includes the ZONEVERSION bytes 02 00 78 95 a4 e9, which the tool displays as SOA-SERIAL: 2023073001 (example.com.). The first byte is the label count of 2, the second is type 0, and the last four are the serial.
sections.eli5: The tool turns the sticker's code into plain words: this answer came from the example.com book, edition 2023073001.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned EDNS(0) option code 19 with the name ZONEVERSION and status Standard. It also created a new "ZONEVERSION TYPE Values" registry. Type 0 is SOA-SERIAL, 1 to 245 are assigned by Specification Required, 246 to 254 are Private Use, and 255 is Reserved.

Mnemonics are uppercase ASCII with a maximum of 15 characters. A designated expert reviews requests and MUST respond within 10 business days.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of edition-number kinds. Number 0 is taken, some numbers are for anyone's private use, and the rest need a written description first.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
EDNS extension data is not covered by RRSIG records, so DNSSEC cannot verify it, and someone in the middle could tamper with it on an insecure transport. The RFC says to take caution and use ZONEVERSION data only for troubleshooting and debugging.

To trust it, use an encrypted and authenticated DNS transport, TSIG or SIG(0). Alternatively, compare a SOA-SERIAL value with a separate SOA query with the DO flag, whose answer is DNSSEC signed, keeping in mind the loose coherency caveat. The SOA serial is already public, so it discloses nothing private.

The option cannot check the correctness of a whole zone. The ZONEMD record in RFC 8976 may be better suited.
sections.eli5: The edition sticker can be faked by someone along the way, so it is good for figuring out what went wrong but not for proving anything.

fields.name: LABELCOUNT
fields.desc: Number of labels of the original QNAME that name the zone.

fields.name: TYPE
fields.desc: Format and meaning of VERSION; 0 is SOA-SERIAL.

fields.name: VERSION
fields.desc: Opaque zone version data; 4 octets for SOA-SERIAL.
